reason: E1 and E2 directly support the premises that dilution and limited mobility in solid precursors kinetically trap a random solid solution in HEA nanoparticles, and that this contrasts with bimetallic systems. However, the cited evidence only addresses synthesis-phase formation, not thermal premelting/melting behavior, so the extrapolation to delayed premelting and sharper melting is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Multi-element dilution in solid precursors restricts atomic mobility and suppresses segregation/ordering
Single-phase HEA nanoparticles form more readily than bimetallic ones under kinetic control
Limited atomic mobility in the solid precursor kinetically traps a random solid solution
This kinetic trapping delays premelting and forces a sharper, higher-temperature melting transition
Bimetallic or single-metal nanoparticles show earlier, more gradual premelting and segregation
